Company: CornerCare Pharmacy

US drugstore chain with 300 neighborhood pharmacies in the Midwest (~6,000 employees). Fills prescriptions (including controlled painkillers and ADHD medicines), gives flu and COVID shots, and sells over-the-counter medicines, vitamins, snacks and household goods. Most prescriptions are paid by Medicare, Medicaid or private insurance. No hospitals or clinics, does not make any drugs, no mail-order.

Rules that APPLY:
- DEA rules for pharmacies that dispense controlled substances (registration, opioids, telehealth prescribing)
- FDA rules on over-the-counter drugs, drug labeling, drug shortages and recalls that reach pharmacy shelves
- Medicare Part D and Medicaid payment and pharmacy rules (CMS)
- CDC vaccine recommendations that change what pharmacists may give
- Patient privacy (HIPAA) and pharmacy recordkeeping
- Workplace and labor rules for retail stores

Rules that DO NOT apply:
- Approval, manufacturing or inspection rules aimed only at drug or device manufacturers
- Hospital, nursing-home, physician-payment or clinical-lab rules
- Research grants, clinical trials, NIH funding notices
- Banking, securities, aviation, energy, farming

[2026-22380] Rule — Health and Human Services Department; Office of the Secretary
Title: Nondiscrimination on the Basis of Disability in Programs or Activities Receiving Federal Financial Assistance
Action: Final rule.
Abstract: The Department of Health and Human Services (HHS or Department) issues this rule to revise the regulation implementing section 504 of the Rehabilitation Act of 1973 (section 504) as it applies to recipients of HHS funding (entitled "Nondiscrimination on the Basis of Disability in Programs or Activities Receiving Federal Financial Assistance," ("2024 Final Rule")), published on May 9, 2024. This rule clarifies that the Department interprets the statutory exclusion of "gender identity disorders not resulting from physical impairments" from the terms "individual with a disability" and "disability" set forth in our regulations to encompass "gender dysphoria not resulting from a physical impairment" for purposes of the regulation. This clarification is necessary to resolve ambiguity introduced in the preamble to the 2024 Final Rule and to ensure compliance with the best reading of the governing statute.

calls.prompt:
Company: CornerCare Pharmacy

US drugstore chain with 300 neighborhood pharmacies in the Midwest (~6,000 employees). Fills prescriptions (including controlled painkillers and ADHD medicines), gives flu and COVID shots, and sells over-the-counter medicines, vitamins, snacks and household goods. Most prescriptions are paid by Medicare, Medicaid or private insurance. No hospitals or clinics, does not make any drugs, no mail-order.

Rules that APPLY:
- DEA rules for pharmacies that dispense controlled substances (registration, opioids, telehealth prescribing)
- FDA rules on over-the-counter drugs, drug labeling, drug shortages and recalls that reach pharmacy shelves
- Medicare Part D and Medicaid payment and pharmacy rules (CMS)
- CDC vaccine recommendations that change what pharmacists may give
- Patient privacy (HIPAA) and pharmacy recordkeeping
- Workplace and labor rules for retail stores

Rules that DO NOT apply:
- Approval, manufacturing or inspection rules aimed only at drug or device manufacturers
- Hospital, nursing-home, physician-payment or clinical-lab rules
- Research grants, clinical trials, NIH funding notices
- Banking, securities, aviation, energy, farming
